what:
CORRECTION (2026-04-27, twice given): there is NO `recalled-ids-<sid>.txt` file. The session tracking file is SOLELY `recalled-paths-<sid>.txt`, which contains BOTH line types in ONE file:
- `file|<abs-path>` lines (encountered files, written by track-recall.sh + self-track-on-fire)
- `ids|<comma-list>` lines (tracked memory IDs, written by SessionStart injection + mergeTrackedIds in trackRecallPost)

Past mistake: in 2026-04-27 Cursor validation I told the user to `cat .aide/cache/recalled-ids-<sid>.txt` to verify the trackRecallPost fix wrote IDs. That file doesn't exist. User had to correct me twice ("dont see recalled ids files" → "Again i told you there are no recalled ids files"). The correct verification is:

```bash
cat /path/to/project/.aide/cache/recalled-paths-<conversation-id>.txt
```

Expected output for a project after a recall:
```
file|/abs/path/to/file.ts
ids|2,3,5,6,7,9,10,11,12,13,15,16
```

Both line types in the same file. NEVER look for `recalled-ids-<sid>.txt` — that path is fictitious. Memory #324 already documents the format but I missed it; reinforcing here so the mistake doesn't recur. Other tracking files in the same .aide/cache/ dir: searched-queries-<sid>.txt (separate file), correction-pending-<sid>.txt (separate flag file), stop-count-<sid>.txt (separate counter), config-mtime.txt (project-level, not session-keyed). Verify file existence with `ls .aide/cache/` before assuming filenames.
why: User had to correct me twice on this in 2026-04-27 Cursor validation. The tracking file structure is documented in memory #324 but in a long block where it's easy to miss. Storing as a sharp standalone correction so future "where do tracked IDs live?" queries surface the right answer immediately. Pattern that should have caught the mistake earlier: when citing a file path, run `ls` first.
